headline: Millions gather in Tehran as Iran bids farewell to Ali Khamenei
summary: Huge crowds filled the Grand Mosalla complex for the second day of funeral ceremonies for the late supreme leader, who was killed in an airstrike on February 28.
details: Millions of mourners gathered at Tehran's Grand Mosalla complex on Sunday for funeral prayers for Iran's late supreme leader Ali Khamenei. Authorities expect more than 10 million people to participate in the ceremonies across the capital.
Khamenei, who ruled the Islamic republic from 1989, was killed at age 86 in an airstrike on February 28 during the first day of the US-Israeli war with Iran.
The service was led by 97-year-old Shia cleric Ja'far Sobhani. President Masoud Pezeshkian and parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf were among the senior officials in attendance.
Notably, Khamenei's son and successor, Mojtaba Khamenei, was absent from the public prayers. He is reported to have been wounded in the February 28 attack.
The late leader's coffin was placed alongside those of four relatives also killed in the February strikes, including an infant granddaughter.
The funeral is being viewed internationally as a test of government support following mass protests in January that rights groups say were suppressed with thousands of deaths.
Following Monday's processions in Tehran, the coffin will be moved to Qom on Tuesday, then to Iraq on Wednesday, before final burial in Mashhad on Thursday.
Significant security measures have been implemented in Tehran to manage the crowds and mitigate a heatwave with temperatures expected to reach 40C.
caption:
Over 10 million people are expected to join the farewell ceremonies for Iran's late supreme leader Ali Khamenei in Tehran.

Millions of mourners gathered at Tehran's Grand Mosalla complex on Sunday for funeral prayers for Iran's late supreme leader Ali Khamenei. Authorities expect more than 10 million people to participate in the ceremonies across the capital.

Khamenei, who ruled the Islamic republic from 1989, was killed at age 86 in an airstrike on February 28 during the first day of the US-Israeli war with Iran.

The service was led by 97-year-old Shia cleric Ja'far Sobhani. President Masoud Pezeshkian and parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf were among the senior officials in attendance.

Notably, Khamenei's son and successor, Mojtaba Khamenei, was absent from the public prayers. He is reported to have been wounded in the February 28 attack.

The late leader's coffin was placed alongside those of four relatives also killed in the February strikes, including an infant granddaughter.

The funeral is being viewed internationally as a test of government support following mass protests in January that rights groups say were suppressed with thousands of deaths.

Following Monday's processions in Tehran, the coffin will be moved to Qom on Tuesday, then to Iraq on Wednesday, before final burial in Mashhad on Thursday.

Significant security measures have been implemented in Tehran to manage the crowds and mitigate a heatwave with temperatures expected to reach 40C.

headline_marked: Brazil vs Norway: [[Brazil seek to break 28-year hoodoo]] against Scandinavian side
headline: Brazil vs Norway: Brazil seek to break 28-year hoodoo against Scandinavian side
summary: The Selecao have never beaten Norway in four meetings, with the current Norway coach Stale Solbakken having been part of the side that stunned Brazil in 1998.
details: Brazil faces Norway today at the New York-New Jersey Stadium, aiming to erase an unwanted record: Norway is the only opponent the Selecao have played but never beaten.
In four historical meetings, Brazil has drawn twice and lost twice. This includes a shocking 2-1 defeat in the 1998 World Cup group stage, where Norway coach Stale Solbakken was a player.
Norway enters the match as a dangerous underdog, having recently secured their first-ever World Cup knockout win by edging Ivory Coast 2-1 in the Round of 32.
While Erling Haaland is the primary focus, Brazil striker Matheus Cunha warned that Norway possesses several other dangerous players, many of whom play in the English leagues.
Brazil faces selection challenges, as Lucas Paqueta is out with a hamstring injury. Coach Carlo Ancelotti must now decide if Neymar will return to the lineup after missing the knockout stages.
Raphinha has returned to training, providing Ancelotti with more options in attack, though newcomer Rayan has also impressed the coaching staff.
For Brazil, this match is more than just a quarterfinal spot; it is a chance to finally secure a victory over Norway and continue their pursuit of a record sixth world title.
caption:
Norway is the only team Brazil has ever played but never beaten. Can the Selecao finally break the curse today?

Brazil faces Norway today at the New York-New Jersey Stadium, aiming to erase an unwanted record: Norway is the only opponent the Selecao have played but never beaten.

In four historical meetings, Brazil has drawn twice and lost twice. This includes a shocking 2-1 defeat in the 1998 World Cup group stage, where Norway coach Stale Solbakken was a player.

Norway enters the match as a dangerous underdog, having recently secured their first-ever World Cup knockout win by edging Ivory Coast 2-1 in the Round of 32.

While Erling Haaland is the primary focus, Brazil striker Matheus Cunha warned that Norway possesses several other dangerous players, many of whom play in the English leagues.

Brazil faces selection challenges, as Lucas Paqueta is out with a hamstring injury. Coach Carlo Ancelotti must now decide if Neymar will return to the lineup after missing the knockout stages.

Raphinha has returned to training, providing Ancelotti with more options in attack, though newcomer Rayan has also impressed the coaching staff.

For Brazil, this match is more than just a quarterfinal spot; it is a chance to finally secure a victory over Norway and continue their pursuit of a record sixth world title.
